steps.say: FAST finds a quarter litre of blood in Morrison pouch, and that single finding sorts the unstable patient to theatre.
steps.tx: **FAST** (focused ultrasound) detects **250** mL of free fluid in **Morrison pouch**; **instability** with a positive scan mandates immediate **laparotomy**, whereas stable FAST-positive patients need **contrast CT** to grade the injury first. Speed matters far more than fine detail in shock.

steps.say: A Chance fracture is a seat-belt signature that warns of torn bowel even when the vitals look fine.
steps.tx: **Lap-belt ecchymosis** with a **Chance fracture** (flexion-distraction) of **L1 to L3** flags **mesenteric** and **hollow viscus injury** that needs **laparotomy** even when vitals stay stable. Peritonitis or free fluid without solid-organ injury mandates opening the abdomen. Stable vitals never overrule a concerning abdominal examination.

steps.say: Pelvic fracture bleeding is wrapped and coiled, but a central aortic haematoma is opened without debate.
steps.tx: **Retroperitoneal haematomas** after **pelvic fracture** take a **pelvic binder** plus **angioembolisation**; a central **zone 1** haematoma from **aortic injury** instead needs **exploration**. The binder shuts the pelvic volume to tamponade veins as coils close the named arteries. Enter the abdomen when the central haematoma expands or pulses.

vis.alt: Anatomy of the abdominal, pelvic and retroperitoneal zones after blunt trauma.
vis.caption: Zone 1 bleeds are opened; pelvic zone bleeds are wrapped and coiled. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The stomach in the chest after trauma signals a ruptured diaphragm until surgery proves otherwise.
steps.tx: Left-sided **diaphragmatic rupture** puts the **intrathoracic stomach** on chest film and needs **repair**, since **30** percent **strangulate**; **laparoscopy misses 10** percent in the acute window. Right-sided tears hide beneath the liver, so thoracoabdominal wounds earn direct inspection. Missed injuries declare themselves through sepsis and obstruction.

left.title: Left: seen and sewn

points: Right tear hides under the liver
right.title: Right: hidden and missed

steps.say: Below the reflection the rectum is diverted and drained; above it the hole is simply sewn shut.
steps.tx: **Low rectal injury below the peritoneal reflection** with **faecal soilage** needs **diversion** plus **presacral drainage**; **intraperitoneal wounds** take **primary repair** instead. A diverting loop shields the low repair from ongoing contamination until healing is fully confirmed. Washout alone never substitutes for protecting the low repair.

steps.say: Low-grade renal injuries rest on the ward, but a dead hilum costs the kidney.
steps.tx: **Renal trauma AAST I to III** when stable gets **nonoperative care**; grade **IV** with **urinary extravasation** gets **stenting**, and grade **V** with **hilar avulsion** needs **nephrectomy**. Bed rest with monitoring carries grades one to three, while lost perfusion leaves no kidney worth saving.

steps.say: Most burst bladders leak beside the peritoneum and heal on a catheter; leaks inside the belly need stitches.
steps.tx: **Extraperitoneal rupture** of the **bladder** accounts for **60** percent, usually beside a **pelvic fracture**, and heals with **catheter drainage** for **10 to 14** days; **intraperitoneal** rupture instead needs operative **two-layer repair**. A cystogram confirms healing before the catheter comes out. Intraperitoneal leaks declare themselves through free fluid and chemical peritonitis.

steps.say: Blood and products in equal parts with low pressure targets keep the trauma patient clottable.
steps.tx: **Damage control resuscitation** gives the **massive transfusion** mix: **1 to 1 to 1 red cells**, **plasma** and **platelets**, with **permissive hypotension** to systolic **80 to 90**, limiting **coagulopathy** before **definitive repair**. Crystalloid stays restricted while rewarming corrects the lethal triad. Reassess perfusion continuously as bleeding control proceeds.
